matches.d: Business Area: Corp. Strategy Seniority Level: Mid-Senior level Job Description: At Cloudera , we empower people to transform complex data into clear and actionable insights. With as much data under management as the hyperscalers, we're the preferred data partner for the top companies in almost every industry. Powered by the relentless innovation of the open source community, Cloudera advances digital transformation for the world’s largest enterprises. Job title: Manager, Applied AI Strategy and Operations Job Purpose: As a Manager, Applied AI Strategy and Operations within the Chief Business Officer and GM, Applied AI’s organization, you will lead high-impact, global commercial and operational initiatives with a direct emphasis on accelerating Cloudera 's Private AI growth. Our Applied AI organization is a fast-moving, dedicated group of Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs), Industry & Applied AI Specialists, and business strategy leaders committed to establishing Cloudera as the trusted standard for Private AI in the enterprise. In this high-autonomy, high-trust role, you will act as the strategic and analytical backbone behind our field engineering motions. You will prioritize the right initiatives across our strategic accounts, establish robust governance and operating rhythms, conduct deep-dive portfolio and sales pipeline analyses, and synthesize complex technical and commercial signals into actionable recommendations for Cloudera 's senior leadership. Key responsibilities: Drive Global Governance & Operating Rhythms: Establish, evolve, and manage the programmatic operating rhythm for the global Applied AI organization across AMER, EMEA, and APAC. Lead the monthly business review (MBR) process—from metric gathering and CRM ingestion through deep quantitative analysis and executive synthesis for senior leadership. Manage the AI Adoption Funnel: Partner with regional FDE and Applied AI Specialist leadership to track, analyze, and optimize customer progression through our four core execution stages: Discovery & Strategy, Solution & Value, Pilot & Prove, and Production & Scale. Account Prioritization & Use Case Frameworks: Structure analytical frameworks grounded in real customer signal—joining technical discovery sessions, reviewing triage outcomes, and working directly with field engineering teams to filter and isolate high-ROI Private AI workloads. Conduct rigorous analyses to down-select and prioritize target accounts across our Top 100 strategic enterprise lists. Define & Standardize Strategic Metrics: Collaborate with central Revenue Operations and AI GTM Sales Strategy to define, refine, and standardize key performance indicators around subscription and consumption-based Private AI adoption. Track organizational progress against critical milestones, including customer pitch meetings, on-site Use Case Workshops, Applied AI Hands-on Labs, and deployed production solutions. Ecosystem & Commercial Strategy: Analyze and support go-to-market operational alignment with major AI infrastructure and ecosystem partners (including NVIDIA Blueprints and VAST). Evaluate revenue share models, joint sales plays, and co-deployment strategies to maximize platform pull-through and annual recurring revenue (ARR) expansion. Cross-Functional Leadership & Solution Productization: Act as an embedded, highly trusted thought partner to technical and commercial leaders. Design and implement scalable processes for tracking team allocations and solution productization, ensuring repeatable delivery patterns are codified and communicated across Account Executives, Solution Engineers, and Professional Services globally. Business Planning & Executive Storytelling: Build comprehensive segment analyses, growth models, and strategic business cases to support critical investment decisions, headcount planning, and resource allocation across regional pods. Preferred Qualifications: Strong problem-solving and structuring skills, with a proven ability to scope complex, ambiguous strategic challenges and identify root causes within technical go-to-market organizations. Highly analytical and excellent at leveraging facts, CRM data, and customer insights to generate and validate strategic hypotheses regarding enterprise AI adoption and workload consumption. Proven ability to communicate and build trust with stakeholders at all levels—including C-suite executives, technical engineering leaders, and regional sales VPs—by turning granular data and research into actionable insight and a well-structured executive storyline. Deep familiarity with enterprise data management platforms, hybrid cloud architectures, data lakehouses (e.g., Apache Iceberg), and the broader AI/ML ecosystem capabilities. Strong quantitative, financial modeling, and data manipulation skills; proficiency in GTM systems (e.g., Salesforce, Clari), business intelligence tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI), and SQL is a strong plus. Demonstrated capacity to operate with high autonomy in dynamic, fast-moving environments, building structure and operational rigor from the ground up rather than inheriting legacy processes. Preferred Experience: 6+ years of progressive work experience in sales strategy, revenue operations, business operations, or management consulting, with a demonstrated track record of driving cross-functional alignment and measurable business impact. Direct experience supporting specialized technical sales, pre-sales, or post-sales delivery teams—particularly within Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE), Solution Architecture, or Applied AI Specialist organizations. Deep domain experience in enterprise software, big data analytics, machine learning/AI, or hybrid cloud infrastructure companies. Proven expertise working with cloud subscription, consumption-based (usage-driven), or product-led growth (PLG) business models, specifically tracking workload transition from pilot to production scale. Experience supporting enterprise commercial or technical organizations through rapid 2–3x+ revenue growth periods and global expansion across AMER, EMEA, and APAC regions. Note: Candidates without direct commercial ownership experience will still be strongly considered if they demonstrate long, deep tenure supporting commercial or technical sales leaders in a closely comparable enterprise GTM model. The right person in this role has an opportunity to make a huge impact at Cloudera and add value to our future decisions. If this position has piqued your interest and you have what we described - we invite you apply! This role is not eligible for immigration sponsorship. The anticipated annual base salary range for this position is: Washington: $144,000 - $162,000 New York: $144,000 - $162,000 California: $144,000 - $162,000 Individual compensation within the published range is determined by the candidate's skills, experience, qualifications, and primary work location. In addition to base pay, sales roles are eligible for Cloudera 's commission plan, while non-sales roles are eligible for the corporate incentive plan. All employees receive a comprehensive benefits package What you can expect from us: Generous PTO Policy Support work life balance with Unplugged Days Flexible WFH Policy Mental & Physical Wellness programs Phone and Internet Reimbursement program Access to Continued Career Development Comprehensive Benefits and Competitive Packages Paid Volunteer Time Employee Resource Groups EEO/VEVRAA LI-SF1 Originally posted on Himalayas

matches.d: About Hostie Hostie is your restaurant’s Virtual Concierge, making sure every call, text, or question gets answered in your voice. Behind the scenes, we handle guest communication, reservations, events, and takeout automatically, all in one place. Hostie takes care of the noise so your staff can focus on the service. Restaurants across North America use Hostie to ensure no guest goes unanswered while giving their teams more time to focus on hospitality. Hostie integrates with platforms like OpenTable, Toast, and SevenRooms and is backed by Gradient Ventures (Google’s AI fund), Obvious Ventures (founded by Ev Williams), and leading hospitality investors. What You'll Do: GTM Strategy & Execution Build and iterate GTM playbooks - messaging, positioning, and launch processes that scale as we identify new product opportunities, new verticals, and new markets. Run competitive analysis and market research to inform how we build our positioning and messaging. Partner closely with sales and customer success to develop and test expansion and growth strategies. Investor & Board Strategy Own preparation for quarterly board meetings - pulling together materials, metrics, and narrative in partnership with the CEO. Field ad hoc investor requests and reports and support fundraising initiatives and investor communications as needed. Build business cases for new initiatives, partnerships, or investments. Business & Finance Operations Partner with Leadership on company priorities, strategic initiatives, and planning cycles. Identify operational gaps and help drive process improvements wherever something is manual, inconsistent, or breaking as we scale. Build and maintain operational metrics, dashboards, and KPI frameworks to track business performance. Support financial forecasting and modeling - helping build and maintain the models Leadership uses to plan headcount, revenue, and spend. Support billing reconciliation and help keep accounts payable running cleanly as we scale. We're Looking For: 2-5+ years of experience in strategy & operations or business operations, ideally in a high-growth tech or startup environment Background from top consulting, investment banking, or a strong business school foundation Analytically sharp instincts — you can build a model, read the data yourself, and don't wait for someone else to distill it A track record of owning something end-to-end, from strategy through execution, not just advising on it Exceptional curiosity and grit — you dig until you actually understand the problem Comfort operating in ambiguity — no one is handing you a playbook here Strong communication and writing ability — you can write a memo for the CEO and hold your own on a call with a merchant or investor A bias toward action and ownership — you'd rather test the hypothesis than write the memo about testing it Fluency with AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, or similar) as part of how you actually work day to day — to move faster, not just polish emails Why Join Us: You'll gain direct exposure to the core functions of building a venture-backed startup: company strategy, GTM execution, operations, fundraising, and strategic partnerships — working alongside the CEO and Leadership Team from an early stage. A fast-growing market, and a chance to make a real impact: The restaurant technology space is expanding quickly, driven by rising demand for digital operations, reservations, and guest experience tools - and restaurants are under more pressure than ever to modernize. You'll join a lean, high-growth team where your work directly shapes how restaurants run better and where individual contributions have outsized impact on the business and the success of the customers we support. Collaborative environment: You'll receive support and guidance from experienced colleagues and managers, helping you learn, grow, and achieve your personal/professional goals. What Else You Need to Know: The yearly total cash compensation for this role is $120k - $140k. Actual compensation will be determined on an individual basis and will vary depending on location, experience, skills, and qualifications. Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package - full-time positions are also eligible for equity awards and benefits. Hostie is a remote-first company. Our HQ is in San Francisco, CA but our team is fully distributed with no onsite requirements. Originally posted on Himalayas

matches.d: Who We Are Everyday Electric (formerly Renew Home) is on a mission to change how we power the world by making it easier for customers to save energy and money at home as part of the largest residential virtual power plant in North America. We partner with industry-leading brands to better manage residential energy for users by prioritizing efficiency, savings, and comfort — and cleaner energy for everyone. We are an Equal Opportunity employer striving to create a diverse, equitable, and inclusive work environment where everyone feels that they have a voice that is heard. We strongly encourage candidates to check out our website at to learn more about the world-changing work we are doing. Role Summary Everyday Electric is hiring a Senior Technical Program Manager to own the planning, execution, and operational health of complex, cross-functional programs across our VPP platform and consumer energy products. This role sits within the Technical Program Management team, reporting to the Director of Technical Program Management, and operates with significant independence to define how programs are structured, tracked, and delivered. This is not a coordination role. The TPM at this level is expected to build and own the frameworks that make execution reliable, communicate tradeoffs and risks in ways that drive decisions, and serve as an operational and technical thought partner to Engineering and Product leadership. Significant cross-functional situational awareness is required -- this person will regularly work across Engineering, Product, Design, Business Development, Customer Success, Grid Operations, and strategic planning functions. What You Will Do Lead end-to-end delivery of complex, multi-team programs spanning Engineering, Product, and Design, from scoping through launch and operational handoff. Define and maintain the planning frameworks, milestone structures, and risk models that enable predictable delivery across your programs -- not just track against plans others set. Identify, escalate, and drive resolution of cross-functional dependencies, blockers, and tradeoffs with clear recommendations, not just status updates. Partner with Engineering and Product leadership to set and pressure-test roadmap sequencing, resource assumptions, and launch readiness criteria. Drive programs through the full product lifecycle, with particular focus on launch readiness, post-launch metric validation, operational handoff to sustaining teams, and ensuring downstream stakeholders -- including Business Development, Customer Success, Grid Operations, and partner-facing functions -- are informed, equipped, and ready to operate before a program is formally closed. Develop and share operational practices and retrospective learnings that raise the execution standard across the broader TPM team. Serve as a decision-support resource for your stakeholders -- synthesizing technical and schedule complexity into clear options and tradeoffs for leadership. Maintain cross-functional situational awareness across interdependent programs, surfacing risks and misalignments before they become escalations. Requirements 7+ years of Technical Program Management or Engineering Program Management experience, with at least 3 years managing programs that span multiple engineering teams. Demonstrated ability to build or substantially improve program management systems and frameworks, not just operate within existing ones. Strong technical (software and/or hardware) foundation -- sufficient to pressure-test engineering estimates, understand architectural tradeoffs, and engage credibly with senior engineers. Track record of driving alignment across functions without formal authority, particularly in environments where priorities compete and stakeholders span technical and non-technical functions. Clear, direct communicator who can translate program complexity into executive-level narratives and decision points. Experience with consumer-facing software products. Preferred: Experience in energy, grid services, IoT, or related infrastructure-adjacent domains. Familiarity with VPP, demand response, or utility partner integration programs. Experience managing programs that involve external partners, device fleets, or regulated operational environments. Benefits What You'll Get A full-time position, with a competitive salary based on experience. The base salary for this role is $185k - $225k. In addition to base compensation, this role is eligible for a target annual bonus of 20% of base salary, and participation in long-term incentive programs tied to company growth and performance. We use market data and consider your job family, background, skills, experience, and U.S. work location to determine compensation within our established pay range. Fully remote work environment with home office set-up allowance. Real and lived work-life balance - Company perks include no pre-set vacation limits (with a top-down culture of taking meaningful PTO every year!), parental leave benefits, and a corporate value of working sustainably and putting families first. Competitive benefits package that includes numerous health and wellness benefits. 401(k) plan, with employer contributions to the same. Opportunity to work with amazing people who are passionate about their mission, thriving in a fully-remote work environment, and learning and growing every day. At this time, Everyday Electric is unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas. Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without current or future immigration from the company, including training plans for foreign students. matches.d: What success looks like in this role: The rise of AI has caused a fundamental shift in the workplace. The organizations that lead this transition won’t win by doing the old job faster, they will win by embracing the change and rethinking the job entirely. Often, this work is split in two: giving people access to and training on the tools, and separately trying to manage the change. You'll support both halves of the problem: the curriculum that builds people's ability to know when and how to work with AI, and the operating model that turns that judgment into an adopted, governed, and measured practice across the organization. You’ll need to think both strategically and tactically. Some days present a high-level, multi-year strategy question; other days, it's working with one team on one workflow to figure out together what "working differently" means today. Both halves are held to the same bar: driving business impact and improving the daily lives of our employees. Key responsibilities: Define and deploy, globally. Map how the work is done today, end-to-end, pinpointing opportunities for AI integration across organizations (such as internal operations, client delivery, pre-sales, and product). Collaboratively define adoption and governance operating models. Help design the model, sponsorship, measurement, feedback loops, guardrails, as part of a broader team effort, and help drive how it runs while minimizing resistance and disruption. Drive AI fluency as a durable capability. Oversee the creation of scalable learning experiences that give people real judgment about delegation, discernment, and diligence with AI, model-agnostic. Support practical upskilling. Oversee the creation and/or curation of resources that ensure that people have the functional ability to leverage AI in the flow of work. Contribute to Unisys presales success. Shape custom Organizational Change Management (OCM) and training strategies that win client pursuits and ensure long-term adoption. Think strategically in terms of what the organization’s work might look like in five years, and also in terms of the specific exercise, workflow, or conversation that needs to happen now to move toward it. Measure behavior and prove it’s worth it. Define what changed practice looks like for each audience and tie adoption back to real business outcomes and to the actual work lives of the people doing the work. Stay ahead of the curve. Track how AI capabilities, tools, and norms are shifting over time, and revise curriculum and guardrails before they go stale. Provide change management support across various initiatives and projects and for broad segments of the organization. Drive processes to ensure key stakeholders understand the change implications associated with outcomes and deliverables. Identify and work with stakeholders to develop and implement strategies that help them thrive in continuous change. Ensure change enablement strategies and actions are incorporated into technology implementations and steady state operations. Play a key role helping to define and measure success metrics and monitor progress as well as business outcomes. You will be successful in this role if you have: BA/BS degree and 6-8 years’ relevant experience OR equivalent combination of education and experience Prosci Certified Change Practitioner, or equivalent OCM certification preferred You may be a good fit if you: Have originated a team or function that didn't exist before. Have successfully deployed AI-forward initiates that drive transformation across an enterprise organization. matches.d: Tremendous is the global platform built for businesses to send thousands of payouts to anyone, anywhere, for free. We're trusted by 20,000 organizations like Atlassian, MIT, and United Way to deliver gift cards and money to millions of recipients worldwide. Our customers (researchers, marketers, HR teams, nonprofits, and platform businesses) rave about how fast and easy Tremendous is to use. Check out our ratings on G2 . Tremendous is profitable and growing without outside investors. We’re a fully remote, high-documentation, low-meeting culture, which means more time for what matters in both your professional and personal life. The team agrees– our employee NPS is in the high 80s. About the role Most PMs at Tremendous run a squad. This role owns problems instead. We're growing fast and spinning up new product areas. Each one needs research, a roadmap, and shovel-ready specs before we staff it. That's your job. You'll dig into areas where we might launch a squad, and run projects too small to need one. You'll carry one or two projects at a time, drawn from the company's highest-priority open questions. When a problem proves worth solving, what happens next depends on how big the opportunity is. If it justifies a long-term team, you'll likely build that squad and lead it as its PM. If it's worth building but smaller, you'll build it yourself with an engineer or two and design help from a related squad. If it's small and close to an existing squad's work, you'll hand it off with a finished brief, and that squad's PM will carry it forward. You'll have real influence over new project areas and which teams exist a year from now. Today, the product management org is 7 PMs, led by a co-founder who serves as Head of Product. You will Report to our Co-founder / Head of Product, Kapil Kale Own new product areas before they have a team. Develop a thesis, do the research, size the opportunity, and make a recommendation: spin up a squad, build it lean, hand it off, or kill it. Kill calls are as valuable as green lights. Turn research into shovel-ready work. Your output is briefs, prototypes, and specs that a squad can pick up and build immediately. Move quickly using AI. Use agents to dig through customer tickets, sales calls, usage data, and competitor research. Ship clickable prototypes in days to test ideas with real customers. Run projects that don't need a full squad. Some work is worth doing but too small for a team. You'll drive these end-to-end with engineers from existing squads. Cover a squad when needed. If a team is temporarily without a PM, you may step in. This is occasional, and your portfolio comes first. Work async. Most product work here happens in writing. If you're used to running product through meetings, this will feel different. You have 6+ years building and shipping web applications as a designer, engineer, or product manager at tech companies, with at least 2 years taking new products from zero to one. Comfortable being the only person accountable for an initiative that doesn't have a team yet. Comfortable owning a portfolio instead of a single product. If validation kills your thesis, you move to the next bet without drama. A track record of turning ambiguous opportunities into prioritized, shovel-ready roadmaps. Strong product intuition, design judgment, and technical fluency. You hold your own with designers and engineers. Outstanding written communication. We're documentation-first, and this role runs on briefs and decision memos that need to persuade senior stakeholders. Founder, founding PM, or first-product-hire experience is a strong plus. What’s cool about the role Competitive pay and equity. Base salary for this role: $250,000 to $325,000. Real benefits. 100% covered health (US), unlimited PTO, 12-16 weeks paid parental leave. Fully remote. Work from anywhere in the Americas. Great culture. Read more about how we work in our public handbook .

matches.d: About Karbon Karbon is the global leader in AI-powered practice management software for accounting firms. We provide an award-winning cloud platform that helps tens of thousands of accounting professionals work more efficiently and collaboratively every day. With customers in 40 countries, we have grown into a globally distributed team across the US, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the Philippines. We are well-funded, ranked #1 on G2, growing rapidly, and have a people-first culture that is recognized with Great Place To Work® certification and on Fortune magazine's Best Small Workplaces™ List. Karbon is further ahead on AI adoption than most companies our size. Every department is running AI daily. Hundreds of skills and workflows have been built by our own team. Fourteen department champions drive adoption and share knowledge across the business. The foundation is real and it works. The next phase is scale. We need one person whose entire job is extending what we have built, measuring what it returns, and adding the next layer of capability. Not a strategy deck. A working system, the governance that makes it trustworthy, and the numbers that prove it. You will report into the CEO and work across every department. You will have the access and sponsorship to make changes stick. About the Role Build the Tooling Ship internal automations and agents that remove repeated manual work across Sales, CS, Implementation, Support, and Operations. Connect AI to the systems we already run, through APIs and MCP servers. The first build is the data gateway. Karbon runs its own MCP server. You extend it into a routing proxy that sits between Claude and every internal data source teams need. Authentication via Okta. RBAC enforcement by department. Request logging for spend attribution and audit. Once the gateway is approved by Security, new connectors plug into a config entry instead of triggering a full review each time. That is your first thirty days. After that: CS gets a renewal risk signal. Sales gets a proposal draft automation. Implementation gets a SOW generator with scope-creep flags. Support gets a ticket triage router. Prototype fast. Harden what people use. Delete what they ignore. Hand every tool to an owner in the team that uses it. You build it. They run it. Own Governance and Visibility Manage the Claude access and provisioning workflow — seat requests, model and tool access, connector approvals — and the Slack workflows that support it. Run the connector security review pipeline in partnership with Security. Own the spend dashboard across all AI tools, not just Claude. Cursor, Codex, Linear AI, and anything else the org is running sit alongside Claude in one view. Department leaders see their own number weekly without asking you to pull it. Bad trends surface before they become invoice surprises. Extend that visibility into an ROI framework: adoption rate, hours saved, cost per seat, project-level impact. Partner with Finance on budget accountability. Run the AI champions program. Fourteen department champions, organized into pods, own peer enablement and skill submissions within their teams. You run the cadences, maintain the hub pages, and hold champions accountable for engagement. When people leave Karbon, their projects and skills do not leave with them. You own the offboarding flow that captures and reassigns that work. Build and maintain the AI wiki — per-department documentation of tools, active use cases, and skills in use. Keep it current as tools evolve. Train Teams and Set the Standard Work with each department lead to agree how their team uses AI, then hold that standard. Run practical training. Short, specific, and repeatable. Teach people the efficient way to get the same answer. Most cost problems are habit problems. After month one, you know what each team's workflows look like because you built them. That makes you a better trainer than anyone who has not. Build and maintain a shared library of prompts, skills, and patterns so knowledge stays when a person leaves. Own the pipeline that moves skills from intake through review to the shared library — and automate the parts of it that should not require a human. Measure and Report the Return Define the small set of metrics that show whether AI is working: cost, adoption, delivery, and quality. Build the data pipelines behind those metrics. Expect the source data to be messy. Publish a regular report to the executive team. Same format every time. Bad news included. Delete any metric that has not changed a decision in a quarter. About You! You shipped production software in the last two years, as the person writing the code. Python or TypeScript, SQL, and REST APIs. You built something real on top of a large language model. Not a demo. Something with users, error handling, and a cost you had to control. You worked directly with non-technical teams as the technical person in the room. Forward deployed engineer, solutions engineer, GTM engineer, internal tools engineer, or similar. You know what a CS renewal motion looks like and what implementation scoping feels like. You do not need to have worked in those roles. You need to have built something those teams actually used. You can build a number out of messy data and defend it to a CFO. You have run a cross-functional program where the participants did not report to you — a champion network, an ambassador program, an adoption initiative. You know how to create accountability without authority. You write clearly, and you can say no to work that will not pay off. Bonus Points: Accounting, professional services, or B2B software market experience. Familiarity with MCP server development, Claude API, or agent frameworks. Experience with Okta or similar identity providers. What Success Looks Like! By month six: Three automations run in production, each owned by the team that uses it. Every department leader can see their own AI usage and cost, including spend outside Claude. The spend dashboard is live and trusted. Your first report to the executive team is argued with, not just acknowledged. The gateway has Security sign-off and every new connector goes through it. By month twelve: Cost per unit of work delivered is moving in the right direction, and everyone agrees on how it is calculated. Three departments extend and run their own tools without you. New starters learn our way of working with AI as part of onboarding. Champion pods are submitting and reviewing skills without you in the loop. The AI wiki is maintained by department owners, not by you. Why Work at Karbon? Gain global experience across Australia, New Zealand, UK, and Canada Strong benefits package including: Flexible Time Off with an encouraged 4 weeks use per year Company paid medical for you and eligible spouse/partner and dependents Paid dental and vision and eligible spouse/partner and dependents 401(k) with company matching Flexible Spending Account Up to 8 weeks paid parental leave Work-from-home stipend Work with (and learn from) an experienced, high-performing team A collaborative, team-oriented culture that embraces diversity, invests in development and provides consistent feedback Be part of a fast-growing company that firmly believes in promoting high performers from within As we hire across various locations within the USA we are required by law to include a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. While we believe competitive compensation is a critical aspect of you deciding to join us, we do hope you also spend time considering why our mission, purpose and values are right for you. We are creating something transformational here, and we hope you are as excited about the future as we are! matches.d: Hi, I’m John and I’m the Head of Professional Services at Ashby. One of my favorite aspects of Ashby is our operating principle of Continuous Improvement https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/culture/ashbys-operating-principles#8---implement-continuous-improvement. Coupled with our principle of caring deeply about our customers, we often find ourselves wondering, “How can we deliver a more impactful customer experience?”. That’s why I’m thrilled to be hiring for our new Solutions Consultant function! As a member of our growing Professional Services team (within Ashby’s Customer Success organization), you’ll have the opportunity to ensure customers have the technical support they need to fully optimize their use of Ashby, helping them build deeper integrations and more effective workflows. ABOUT THE ROLE This role sits at the intersection of Customer Success, Product, and Support — bridging deep technical acumen with strong customer-facing skills. You’ll serve as a subject matter expert (SME) on complex product areas and integrations, working hands-on with customers via live engagements and expanding our team’s technical delivery capabilities. You’ll bring both product expertise and a consultative mindset, playing a critical role in implementations and integrations. WHAT YOU’LL DO: - Serve as a post-sales technical SME on complex product integrations, including enterprise identity and access management (IAM), workplace integrations, and custom APIs, supporting both internal teams and customers during implementations, early access product releases, and advanced configurations. - Lead customer-facing technical engagements, including discovery sessions, best practice consulting, and hands-on configuration of technical workflows. - Collaborate with Product to surface emerging technical pain points for exploration and stay ahead of new product capabilities that inform our customer engagements. - Enable our Technical Support team to focus on break/fix issues for existing configurations while you work upstream with customers to design and launch those configurations. - Execute solutions explored in pre-sales conversations to ensure continuity between customer expectations and delivered outcomes. - Translate technical depth into scale, converting insights and one-off solutions into documentation, playbooks, tooling, or enablement content for wider reuse when appropriate. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE: - Customers receive enterprise-grade technical guidance and configuration support during implementation and post-live optimization activities - Ashby expands its customer offerings while enabling more effective specialization of responsibilities with cross-functional partners like Product and Support - Professional Services opens new revenue streams via defined technical services offerings - Technical workstreams operate collaboratively with core implementation workstreams and customer success motions - Custom solutions are documented and scaled for use with other customers YOU COULD BE GREAT FOR FIT IT YOU: - Are a technical generalist who can go deep quickly on topics like M365 and Google Workspace configurations and API-driven custom integrations. - Have prior experience as a Solutions Consultant, Sales Engineer, Technical Implementation Specialist, or Product Manager, working with a complex SaaS product. - Can distill complex concepts for functional Talent Acquisition stakeholders (e.g., Recruiting Operations Managers), technical admins (e.g. HRIS or IT stakeholders), and executive decision-makers (e.g. VP of Talent). - Love live customer interaction, and enjoy solving problems in real time with users. - Thrive in ambiguity and are resourceful and self-directed — you’re excited to build the solution if it doesn’t yet exist. - Care deeply about product quality, clarity, and consistency — and want to help us raise the bar through every customer touchpoint. YOU MIGHT NOT BE A FIT IF: - You’re looking for a purely behind-the-scenes role with little customer interaction. - You prefer to specialize in a narrow technical domain rather than working across multiple feature sets. - You want strict role boundaries — this job blends technical depth with customer-facing work, and flexing between both is key. - You’re uncomfortable with ambiguity or iterative problem solving — this role often works in emerging areas without pre-defined solutions. - You rely heavily on handoffs or checklists — success here often requires defining and owning an issue end-to-end, even if it’s messy. OUR PHILOSOPHY Here are a few key points (relevant to the go-to-market side) that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us: - We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is a lot easier to sell. - We want to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers. - We strongly believe that small teams with very talented people (and the right work environment) deliver much better performance than teams with large headcount. We hire and compensate accordingly. - We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over experience, and thoughtful communication (we put a lot of effort into using the right communication channels) - we’ll get into these and other values during the hiring process. THE INTERVIEW At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. Our interview process is structured to get to know you and your career as well as empower you with insight into our key focus areas. Here is the process in its entirety: - 30 min - Recruiter Screen with Talent Team - 45 min - Interview with Head of Professional Services (Hiring Manager) - Take Home Exercise (one week to complete) - 60 min - Interview with Integrations Consultant and Product Manager - Final Round: - 30 min - Interview with VP of Customer Success - 30 min - Interview with CEO - 10 min - Closing Questions with Hiring Manager Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities. Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

ABOUT THIS ROLE: As our next Integrations Consultant, you’ll be responsible for defining, managing, and executing the technical requirements for strategic customers, specifically those implementing Ashby with one of our custom-built HCM integrations. You will work with customers with varying levels of integration sophistication advising on integration best practices, technical configurations, and working with a customer’s internal expert on how to best achieve their goals. You will partner with Product/Engineering, Implementation Specialists, CSMs, Sales Engineers, and other cross functional partners to achieve this. Ideally, this hire would be located in the EST time zone. Role requirements: - Enterprise Human Capital Management (HCM) Integration Experience: You have extensive experience managing and executing integrations with Workday, as well as other enterprise-grade HCM solutions like UKG, ADP, Oracle, and SAP SuccessFactors (defining the work, aligning with stakeholders, communicating the project plan, and ultimately delivering results in accordance with the agreed upon expectations). You keep the team on track to ensure milestones are met. We’d love it if you have a Workday HCM certification. Even better if you’ve also managed integrations with tools listed under Integrations on our Ashby Knowledge Base https://ashbyhq.notion.site/. - Customer Centricity: You are adept at understanding customer needs and tailoring implementations to meet their specific requirements. You build strong customer relationships by maintaining high levels of engagement and communication; you’re the customer’s proactive guide and advocate throughout the implementation period. - Change Management: You are experienced in navigating change management processes and helping customers adapt to new systems and a refreshed approach. - Technical Proficiency: You have a solid understanding of a complex product (ideally Ashby) and its technical intricacies; you are technically curious and creative. - Consultative: You take pride in advising customers on best practices specific to their usage of software to ensure optimal value. - Innovative & Principled: You proactively address thematic customer opportunities and improve our processes accordingly. You don’t rely on ‘I’ve seen this done’ but instead think critically to solve problems. - Cross-functional Collaboration: You effectively partner with cross-functional stakeholders across Customer Success, Sales, Product, Engineering, and Operations to align and define progress. Understanding of REST APIs, CRMs, data pipelines, and sales/marketing automation tools , with the ability to design scalable, integration-rich solutions. Cross-functional operator — partners effectively with Sales, Onboarding, CS, Product, and Engineering to deliver measurable customer outcomes. matches.d: Introduction Join us at AIT, where we believe every day presents an opportunity to make a global impact! We’re problem solvers, driven by our curiosity and creativity, in endless pursuit of solutions for our customers. Together, we champion the strength of our global teams. And, as trusted advisors, we go above and beyond, working together in a supportive and collaborative environment to ensure customer satisfaction. Through the company's continued growth, we challenge ourselves to be better, continuously learning and growing in our dynamic environment. Helping others is at the core of our culture, join us in finding fulfillment by giving back to our local communities as the united team that is AIT. Find out what our people deliver.® means when you come move the world with us! Hear directly from our teammates at AIT Worldwide Logistics and make us the next stop on your career journey. Overview The Business Systems Analyst will support all areas of IT by understanding the diverse business need and product offerings, as well as the technology systems that support our business. This position will primarily focus on our customers’ business needs and offer products and/or solutions to meet those needs. Responsibilities Working with customers and/or business stakeholders to accurately capture business requirements for new projects and customer onboarding Work with IT team members to review and clarify requirements as needed and act as the liaison between business project stakeholders and IT Responsible for technical documentation of system components and processes Maintains and manages customer service requests that are routed via our Service Desk Manages and monitors existing functionalities and defines new functionality as needed for application integrity Interfaces with internal and external technical staff to define application solutions and resolve problems as needed Manage incident workflow from initial reporting to final resolution including incident handoffs with outsourced 3rd party organizations Collaborate with IT to develop detailed project specifications Conduct testing and deliver training related material for new customer IT enhancements Contribute to a knowledge base of known problems and resolutions for customers and sales to resolve problems on their own Other duties and responsibilities as assigned. Qualifications A team player who works well with others – being respectful to our teammates is a Core Value A strong work ethic with an appreciation for ownership, independence, accountability, and autonomy in your role Growth mindset – being passionate about your craft, always looking for ways to improve yourself and the company, being open to change and doing things differently Customer service focus – we serve a wide variety of customers, both internal and external, and building relationships is a part of our culture Other Skills We Hope to See: Minimum 5 years related work experience and / or training Ability to effectively present and promote technology and respond to questions from groups of managers, customers, and co-workers Work with customers to resolve their business problems or inefficiencies using technology and business process Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization exists What AIT Can Offer You In addition to your base compensation, you may be eligible for a bonus based on achievement of business and/or individual performance metrics (dependent on position). Benefits offered include Medical, Prescription, Health Savings Account, Flexible Spending Accounts, Dental, Vision, Life, AD&D, Disability, Supplemental Health, Employee Support, Paid Parental Leave, Pet Insurance, 401(k) and Tuition Reimbursement. In addition, teammates may be eligible for up to 10 to 20 days of vacation (depending on tenure), 2 personal days, 1 floating holiday, 5 sick days, 5 volunteer hours, and 6 company holidays (plus Veterans Day for Veterans) annually. About AIT Worldwide AIT Worldwide Logistics is a global freight forwarder that helps companies grow by expanding access to markets all over the world where they can sell and/or procure their raw materials, components and finished goods. For more than 40 years, the Chicago-based supply chain solutions leader has relied on a consultative approach to build a global network and trusted partnerships in nearly every industry, including aerospace, automotive, consumer retail, energy, food, government, high-tech, industrial, life sciences and marine. Backed by scalable, user-friendly technology, AIT’s flexible business model customizes door-to-door deliveries via sea, air, ground and rail—on time and on budget. With expert teammates staffing more than 150 worldwide locations in Asia, Europe and North America, AIT’s full-service options also include customs clearance, warehouse management and white glove services. AIT Worldwide Logistics is an Equal Opportunity Employer – M/F/Veterans/Disabled. If you are unable to apply online due to a disability, contact Human Resources at 630-766-8300 ext 5218. matches.why: Good match for candidate's cross-functional technical project delivery, customer onboarding, and systems coordination background.
matches.d: Role Summary Ciroos is hiring a Technical Customer Success / Customer Program Manager to own the customer program from onboarding through adoption — connecting the dots across the customer, Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE), Product, and Engineering. This is a role for someone who knows how to drive: you'll know what needs to happen, who owns it, what's blocked, what needs to be prioritized, and what comes next to keep the customer moving forward. You'll be the person making sure things don't fall through the cracks. You need enough technical depth to be comfortable working with SRE, observability, cloud, infrastructure, integrations, and enterprise IT teams — but you are not expected to be the FDE building everything yourself. Your job is to make the entire program move. What You'll Do Program Ownership & Cross-Functional Orchestration Own the customer program end-to-end from onboarding through adoption, tracking what needs to happen, who owns it, what's blocked, and what to prioritize next. Drive accountability across teams: when Engineering owes something, you drive it to closure; when Product needs to make a decision, you get it in front of them; when priorities compete, you help create clarity. Coordinate complex, multi-stakeholder technical deliverables to a clean finish — for example, driving an enterprise security questionnaire (such as a Splunk-integration review covering data retention, permissions, token encryption, and incident response) from a draft with open “pending engineering confirmation” items to a fully-owned, sign-off-ready response, assigning clear owners and chasing each item to closure. Maintain a single source of truth on program status — open items, owners, and dates — so nothing depends on memory or gets lost between Slack threads, docs, and meetings. Customer Relationship & Value Delivery Build strong relationships with customers, understand what success looks like for them, and keep them engaged throughout onboarding and adoption. You've either worked as a project manager inside a medical device or clinical organization, run large ERP or supply-chain implementations, or led enterprise-level SaaS implementations in the Life Sciences or Healthcare IT space. Either way, you speak the language of the clients we serve, and you bring real rigor to how you manage a program. You’ve also worked somewhere fast-moving and not fully formal, and you know how to adapt your process to fit rather than importing a rigid framework. You don’t wait for internal clarity before acting with confidence. You hold the line on scope, timeline, and rigor with clients and with your own team, even while the environment around you is still being defined. You’re comfortable being the senior voice in the room with a client, and just as comfortable pushing back internally when something isn’t set up to succeed. A confident, credible presence: clients and internal teams see you as someone who can hold the line on scope, timeline, and rigor, even before every internal process is fully defined. You don’t wait for top-down clarity to act. Process oriented approach: you’ve adapted PM process and status-reporting cadence to fit Movemedical ’s actual pace and stage, building something repeatable rather than importing a framework wholesale, so the rigor doesn’t depend on any one person’s habits. Judgment under pressure: you’ve correctly judged when a real risk needed to go to your manager versus being handled independently, and you’ve stayed effective through sustained ambiguity or internal politics without disengaging. Trusted by clients and colleagues alike: you’ve built genuine credibility with med device and clinical client stakeholders, translating product and technical reality into plans they can trust, even when things weren’t going smoothly. Experience as a project manager inside a medical device or clinical organization, running large ERP / supply-chain implementations (e.g., SAP), or leading enterprise-level SaaS implementations in the Life Sciences or Healthcare IT space. Industry exposure is valued, not required. A track record of running complex, multi-stakeholder implementation programs end-to-end, with real scoping, timeline, and risk-tracking discipline Demonstrated ability to adapt a PM process you know well to a faster-moving, less formal environment, rather than importing it wholesale Comfortable holding a position and pushing back, whether with clients or with your own leadership, even under ambiguity or pressure Strong written and verbal communication, with the judgment to know when to escalate a risk and when to handle it yourself You're comfortable traveling up to approximately 25% of the time, as needed, to support client engagements Is this the right role for you? This is likely a strong fit if: You’ve worked inside a medical device, clinical, or complex enterprise-implementation environment (SAP or similar) and speak that world fluently You’d rather adapt your process to a fast-moving company than import a playbook wholesale from a more structured one You hold your ground with clients and with your own leadership, and you’re comfortable acting before every detail is settled You want real ownership of programs from day one, not a process someone else already built It may be less of a fit if: You do your best work when a company already has a mature, well-established process to step into, and you're less drawn to learning the operational ins and outs of medical device or clinical client environments. This role leans heavily on that operational fluency alongside the PM mechanics, so if you'd rather focus purely on the mechanics of the job, it's probably not where you'll do your best work. You prefer a fully defined framework and a larger team to lean on before making a call You are looking for a people-management role. Hungry – You own problems and push beyond expectations without being asked Humble – You value team success over ego and foster shared wins Strong – You are self-aware, coachable, and willing to engage in hard conversations What Do We Offer? Great People: Join a team of hungry, humble, and strong problem solvers dedicated to impacting patient lives around the world. The ideal candidate will be equally comfortable leading new customer implementations and providing strategic post-go-live consulting and optimization services. Strong technical configuration and systems administration experience with the ability to troubleshoot complex customer requirements. Experience implementing AI-powered customer support solutions, chatbots, virtual agents, and voice automation capabilities. Proven ability to understand customer business challenges and translate requirements into scalable platform solutions. Experience facilitating customer workshops, requirements gathering sessions, training, and executive-level presentations. Strong consulting, stakeholder management, and customer-facing communication skills. Ability to manage multiple projects and customer engagements simultaneously. Passion for solving complex business and technical challenges with a commitment to customer success. Nice to Have Experience supporting both implementation and post-go-live managed services engagements. Experience with cloud architecture, VoIP, SIP, telephony, APIs, and integrations. Sprinklr platform experience or experience with a competing CCaaS/CXM platform. Experience implementing AI, chatbot, workforce management, or customer journey orchestration solutions. Experience with Care, Research, Sales, Marketing, Advertising, or broader CXM SaaS platforms. Relevant contact center and cloud certifications. Empower companies to deliver next generation, unified engagement journeys that reimagine the customer experience. Create a culture of customer obsession, with trust, teamwork, and accountability. Demonstrated ability to analyze public companies and synthesize financial, strategic and market information into an investment or strategic point of view. Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint. Ability to structure and solve complex, ambiguous business problems. matches.d: Description About Us Gambit is the AI-native resilience platform that ensures digital continuity never expires. It unifies governance across cloud, backups, security tools, and IaC, mapping applications, identifying gaps, and validating recovery paths in real time. Gambit turns resilience assumptions into business certainty before an incident ever occurs. ﻿The Opportunity As a Senior Technical Account Manager, you own a book of roughly 9 to 15 enterprise accounts end to end, from kickoff through renewal, and you do it independently: your work does not get reviewed before it reaches a customer. You make sure each customer actually gets more resilient with Gambit, can prove it to their board and regulators, and renews and grows. The difference from the level below is judgment. You handle multi-cloud estates, regulated customers, difficult executive conversations, and ambiguous findings without a safety net, and you mentor newer TAMs while making the team's playbooks better. You do not carry a quota; you carry retention, adoption, posture improvement, and the trust of the accounts you own. About the Role Onboarding. Confirm success criteria in writing, drive the implementation plan, and validate business application mapping, criticality tiering, and RTO and RPO targets with the customer. Posture advisory. Translate Gambit findings into prioritized remediation plans tied to business impact, engineering effort, and risk retired, and advise on backup policy, immutability, isolation, and clean recovery paths. Compliance evidence. Build control-level evidence packages for internal audit, external auditors, and regulators across DORA, NIS2, SOX, SOC 2, ISO 27001, and NIST. Executive reviews. Own the quarterly business review with executive sponsors, and produce posture assessments and cost-of-remediation analyses verified against real data. Escalations and renewal risk. Own escalations end to end, including severity-one events; maintain a risk register and renewal readiness assessment for every account; and hand expansion signals to the Account Executive with the technical justification already built. Team and product. Mentor newer TAMs, improve the team's playbooks and templates, and represent customers to Product and R&D with evidence-backed demand. Requirements 7+ years in technical account management, customer success engineering, technical consulting, solutions architecture, or post-sale technical delivery, with at least 3 years owning enterprise accounts directly. Deep working knowledge of at least one major cloud, with hands-on experience across backup and disaster recovery: retention, immutability and WORM, replication, restore point hygiene, and RTO and RPO planning, applied to real enterprise environments rather than in theory. Experience supporting an enterprise customer through an audit or compliance review, producing evidence mapped to controls under at least one of DORA, NIS2, SOX, SOC 2, ISO 27001, or NIST, plus a working understanding of infrastructure as code and how drift happens in practice. Comfortable querying APIs, working with JSON, and building your own analyses without waiting on someone else, with growing use of AI tooling to speed up customer-facing work. A track record of retention and expansion across a book of enterprise accounts, including at least one at-risk account you stabilized. Credible in front of CISOs and infrastructure leaders without support from leadership, with executive-facing deliverables you personally built. Experience mentoring or reviewing the work of peers, and contributing improvements that others on your team adopted. Comfort operating without established process, four years of college-level courses in a technical field or equivalent practical experience, and openness to up to 20% travel. ﻿NICE TO HAVE Experience at a cyber resilience, backup and recovery, data protection, CSPM, or observability vendor, or with platforms such as Veeam, Rubrik, Cohesity, or Commvault Prior hands-on experience as a cloud, infrastructure, SRE, or security engineer Experience working with agentic AI tooling or MCP-based integrations in a customer-facing context ﻿ ﻿Benefits - Why Gambit?﻿ At Gambit, we believe great work starts with great people — and we’re building a team of smart, driven, genuinely great co-workers who enjoy doing big things together. Here’s what you can expect when you join us: OTE ranging from $230,000 - $260,000 (80/20 split) Competitive medical, dental, and vision insurance A $350 work-from-home stipend to create a setup that helps you do your best work Work alongside smart, supportive, and collaborative co-workers who are excited to build something meaningful together ﻿Pay Transparency Disclosure ﻿ Job level and actual compensation will be decided based on factors including, but not limited to, individual qualifications objectively assessed during the interview process (including skills and prior relevant experience, potential impact, and scope of role), market demands, and specific work location. The listed range is a guideline, and the range for this role may be modified. For roles that are available to be filled remotely, the pay range is localized according to employee work location. ﻿EEO Gambit Security is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. The company has delivered more than 15 million sessions of mental health care, published more than 35 peer-reviewed studies, and delivered unmatched outcomes in terms of access, clinical effectiveness, and cost efficiency. Extensive peer-reviewed research confirms Lyra’s transformative care model helps people recover twice as fast and results in a 26% annual reduction in overall healthcare claims costs. Lyra is transforming access to life-changing mental health care through Lyra Empower, the only fully integrated, AI-powered platform combining the highest-quality care and technology solutions. About the Role: Reporting to the VP Strategy, the Market Activation Analyst for Health Plans & Health Systems (HP/HS) will serve as the analytical engine driving strategic geographic expansion, market entry, and commercial activation. This role bridges macro-level healthcare market intelligence with tactical target setting to optimize commercial growth and care delivery scaling. The ideal candidate possesses deep quantitative rigour, experience working with third-party healthcare datasets, and the ability to turn complex market dynamics into executable, provider-level and payer-level activation playbooks. Responsibilities Macro Market Analysis & Expansion Strategy Leverage third-party healthcare data platforms and analytical tools (e.g., claims data, census/demographic data, payer landscape analysis) to conduct macro-level market evaluations. Synthesize complex market trends to inform the corporate roadmap and establish data-driven strategic rationales for future geographic expansion and payer contracting priorities. Evaluate payer density, reimbursement models, and local healthcare regulations to identify high-value market entry opportunities. Playbook Customization & Tactical Prioritization Develop and customize market-specific activation playbooks with directional prioritization of target provider groups, health systems, and specialty service lines. Conduct strategic profiling and market-level competitive analysis to pinpoint high-potential clinical partners and network integration opportunities. Partner with cross-functional commercial, clinical operations, and business development teams to tailor market go-to-market strategies based on local competitive dynamics. Funnel Modeling & Target Setting Refine, maintain, and own the market activation Top-of-Funnel (TOFU) and Care Starts quantitative models that drive company-wide target-setting. Track key performance indicators (KPIs) across activation stages—from initial market entry and provider outreach through to patient onboarding and active care starts. Iterate forecast models using empirical performance data to optimize lead generation, funnel efficiency, and revenue predictability per market. Qualifications Experience: 3+ years of experience in healthcare analytics, management consulting, corporate strategy, business operations, or market intelligence within a digital health, health plan, health system, or high-growth healthtech organization. Data & Analytical Skills: Advanced quantitative and analytical skills (Excel, Google Sheets, SQL, or BI tools like Tableau/Looker) with proven experience structuring and manipulating large third-party datasets (e.g., IQVIA, Definitely Health, CMS/claims data). Strategic & Funnel Modeling: Direct experience building and maintaining conversion, pipeline, or top-of-funnel operational models (e.g., lead-to-care start funnels). Industry Knowledge: Deep understanding of US healthcare delivery models, health plan reimbursement structures, health system operations, and provider profiling. About the Role We are seeking a highly organized and detail-oriented Senior Technical Project Manager (Compliance & Certifications) to coordinate, manage, and drive our technical compliance, security, and industry certification initiatives. In this role, you will be the operational engine behind our compliance roadmap—managing the rigid timelines of external audits while aligning execution across internal software development, IT/TechOps, and business operations cycles. As a key member of our execution team, you will ensure that all compliance projects are structured, tracked, and reported in strict accordance with our corporate PMO Standards. You will directly own and manage the planning, tracking, and execution of our annual Media Rating Council (MRC) accreditation and SOC2 (Type 1 and Type 2) audits. This role provides the critical project management, compliance oversight, governance, and auditability necessary to keep all teams aligned and audit-ready. Key Responsibilities 1. PMO Reporting & Project Standards PMO Standards Alignment: Manage and structure all compliance, security, and certification project plans, trackers, and document repositories in accordance with established PMO methodologies and guidelines. Standardized Status Reporting: Provide routine, structured progress reports, KPI dashboards, and project health updates (covering milestones, risks, and blockers) as defined by PMO reporting frameworks. Risk & Issue Escalation: Actively track dependencies and risks, executing formal escalation paths per PMO standards when compliance milestones are in jeopardy. Platform Management: Maintain up-to-date program trackers, schedules, and resource planning artifacts within central PMO tools (such as Asana or Jira) to ensure a single source of truth. 2. Hybrid Project Management & Governance Milestone & Critical Path Tracking: Establish clear, phase-gate project plans for upcoming audits, mapping out the critical path for audit readiness, dry-runs, evidence lock-down, and formal evaluation windows. Requirements Translation: Translate complex, rigid compliance controls (e.g., security protocols, data-filtering standards) into clear, actionable technical specifications, user stories, and development tasks. Engineering Alignment: Partner with Security, TechOps, Data, and Engineering teams to slot compliance-related tasks and vulnerability remediations into active development cycles (sprints or Kanban) without disrupting the core product roadmap. Cross-Functional Compliance Oversight: Oversee key operational controls managed by technical partner teams to ensure continuous audit readiness. 3. Audit Coordination & Evidence Gathering Audit Liaison: Serve as the primary operational contact and liaison for external auditors and assessors (e.g., MRC, EY, SOC2 auditors), ensuring meetings, requests, and inquiries are managed efficiently. Evidence Management: Project manage the continuous gathering, formatting, and submission of technical evidence (configurations, access logs, architectural diagrams) required for SOC2 and MRC evaluations. Remediation Tracking: Monitor and drive the resolution of any compliance gaps, audit findings, or vulnerability remediation tasks identified during pre-audits or continuous monitoring. 4. Media Rating Council (MRC) Certification Support Audit Lifecycle Management: Project manage the end-to-end timeline for annual MRC audits, pre-assessment phases, and ongoing compliance reviews. Adtech & Measurement Standards: Coordinate engineering and product tasks related to data pipelines, measurement methodologies, and filtration logic to ensure strict alignment with MRC and industry measurement standards. Disclosure & Change Governance: Coordinate the preparation, maintenance, and regular updating of methodology disclosures, and establish a "Journal of Change" process to manage and communicate changes to accredited elements with MRC and auditor representatives. Business Operations Alignment: Project manage compliance workflows across business operations required by MRC standards, including Business Partner Qualification (BPQ/client vetting), client onboarding/support disclosures, and discrepancy/data reissuance tracking. 5. SOC2 Type 1 & Type 2 Support Audit Execution: Organize the schedule, operational execution, and readiness milestones for annual SOC2 Type 1 and Type 2 audits. Controls Integration: Partner with engineering and IT teams to ensure system monitoring, access control reviews, and infrastructure configurations are consistently maintained and documented according to SOC2 Trust Services Criteria. Automation Management: Help manage and monitor compliance automation tooling (e.g., Vanta, Drata) to ensure continuous control verification and evidence tracking. PMO Alignment: Proven experience managing projects and reporting project health, timelines, and status updates in alignment with structured PMO frameworks. Hybrid PM Expertise: Demonstrated ability to manage fixed-deadline, structured compliance timelines (milestone/waterfall approach) while integrating execution into Agile-operating engineering teams. Compliance & Governance: Practical experience managing projects, timelines, evidence gathering, or compliance oversight related to SOC2 audits or Media Rating Council (MRC) accreditation. Project Tracking Platforms: Advanced proficiency in structured project planning and execution tracking within platforms like Asana or Jira. Technical Literacy: Comfort working alongside engineering and IT teams; ability to understand cloud infrastructure concepts (AWS/GCP), database schemas, and identity/access management frameworks. Preferred Qualifications Adtech Background: Deep understanding of ad-serving technology, measurement methodologies, and industry measurement standards. Certifications: PMP (Project Management Professional), CAPM, PMI-ACP, or introductory security/compliance credentials. Compliance Tooling: Experience using compliance automation platforms (e.g., Drata, Vanta, Secureframe) to track control verification and evidence gathering. The agency is implementing a statewide electronic health record (EHR) and Medicaid billing solution for its Medicaid School-Based Services program, equipping school-based practitioners to document services and support Medicaid billing. The Project Manager works within the state's Enterprise Project Management Office (EPMO), follows its hybrid project lifecycle (Agile practices during implementation), and manages the project day to day alongside the state project team and the implementation vendor. Key Responsibilities Create and maintain the project schedule in the EPMO-prescribed tool (activities, dependencies, milestones, resources, percent complete), updated weekly through closeout, and take part in weekly updates to the implementation vendor's master schedule. Deliver weekly project status reports in the state's project management tool. Create and maintain risks and issues, recommend responses, and run monthly risk and issue reviews. Facilitate project meetings, including status, risk/issue review, backlog grooming, release planning and change review; publish agendas 24 hours before and minutes 24 hours after. Track project financials and enter actual expenditures in the EPMO tool monthly or as approved changes affect the budget. Manage change control with the EPMO portfolio manager and state governance committees, using the state's Change Request Form, and track changes in the project tool. Track all deliverables in a deliverable approval matrix and manage the implementation vendor's Deliverable Expectation Documents (DED) and Deliverable Acceptance Forms (DAF). Maintain the stakeholder register, decision log and action item log; engage sponsors and governance committees on policy decisions, scope, resources, budget and escalated issues. Facilitate project activities, including the state's procurement process. Produce deliverables required by state, agency and federal governance (for example CMS), following EPMO templates. Willing to complete HIPAA training after selection and maintain it for the duration of the engagement (not required to apply). Experience managing IT implementation projects for state government, preferably health and human services or Medicaid programs. Experience managing an implementation vendor's schedule and deliverables, including deliverable review and acceptance. Experience with hybrid or Agile delivery, including backlog grooming and release planning. Proficiency with Azure DevOps and Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Project, Visio) and Adobe PDF. Strong organization, document repository management, and written and verbal communication. Available full time, Monday to Friday, 7:45 AM to 4:30 PM Eastern Time. Located in and authorized to work in the United States; W-2 only (no C2C or 1099). Must pass a national criminal background check, sign the client's acceptable use and confidentiality terms, work only on client-provided systems through Azure Virtual Desktop, and not use AI meeting assistants in client meetings. Preferred: EHR, electronic health record, Medicaid billing, MMIS or school-based health services implementation experience. Experience working within a state Enterprise Project Management Office and its templates and governance. Experience producing deliverables for CMS or other federal partner oversight.
