matches.d: About Engine Engine is the AI-native platform for intelligent travel. For a decade, Engine has built the proprietary technology and supply behind modern business travel, serving over 40,000 customers and nearly 2 million travelers, along with leading travel and AI companies that build on Engine's infrastructure. One system powers business travel, group travel, human agents, and AI agents. That work has earned recognition as one of Fast Company's Best Workplaces for Innovators (2025), TravelTech's Reservation Platform of the Year (2026), and one of Built In's Best Places to Work (2020–2026). We're looking for bold, ambitious people to help redefine how businesses manage and experience travel. Working here, you can expect exponential growth, an ambitious pace, full ownership, and high-caliber colleagues who push you to do the best work of your career. Every hire raises the bar. Come outpace the ordinary and build the future of travel with us. Your Mission We are seeking a Senior Product Data Analyst to join the Omni product team. Omni is Engine's hotel booking infrastructure product, built for external companies that want to embed hotel booking directly into their own platform. It delivers Engine's full inventory, pricing, payments, and support through two integration paths: Omni Swift, a low-code hosted storefront that gets partners live in days, and Omni Halo, a full API for companies that want to own the complete booking journey from search to payment. With 1M+ properties across 185+ countries and 30M+ hotel nights already processed on Engine's underlying infrastructure, the data layer here is genuinely rich and complex. Data is a core competency of Engine, and this role sits at the intersection of product development and analytical rigor. You will be embedded directly in the Omni product org, working alongside product managers, engineers, and designers to shape how Omni evolves. This is a high-autonomy role for someone who doesn't wait to be asked, you'll bring insights to the table before anyone thinks to request them, design and run experiments that validate product bets, and translate booking-scale data into decisions the team can act on. What You'll Do • Design, run, and analyze A/B tests and product experiments across the Omni funnel — from hypothesis definition and instrumentation validation through results analysis and recommendation. • Proactively surface insights to product managers: anomalies in booking behavior, partner conversion degradation, funnel drop-offs, and pricing patterns that signal an opportunity — before anyone asks. • Own deep visibility into the Omni search-to-booking funnel; identify where and why partners and travelers drop off, model the impact of product changes on conversion, and connect funnel performance to revenue outcomes. • Build and maintain analytics that track partner performance across Omni Swift and Halo — activation rates, booking volume, revenue share, API health, and feature adoption. • Analyze how real-time pricing, inventory availability, and AI-driven pricing signals affect search quality, conversion, and revenue; surface patterns that inform pricing strategy and product decisions. • Monitor and analyze API and product health metrics — latency, search response quality, error rates, content deduplication effectiveness — and translate technical signals into product and business implications. • Partner closely with Omni PMs as an embedded analytical resource: contribute to PRDs with data, challenge assumptions with analysis, and ensure the analytical voice is present in every product decision and roadmap prioritization. • Leverage advanced SQL to explore large, complex datasets — booking events, search logs, pricing signals, and partner activity — and uncover key insights at scale. • Independently investigate open-ended product and business questions; identify patterns, quantify opportunities, and deliver actionable recommendations to product and senior leadership. • Identify instrumentation gaps and partner with engineering to ensure the right events are captured; collaborate with analytics engineering to build clean, reusable data models that enable self-service analysis across the team. What We're Looking For • Bachelor's degree in Data, Economics, Statistics, Computer Science, Operations Research, or a related quantitative field. • 4+ years of relevant experience in product analytics or data analytics, with meaningful time spent embedded in a product or engineering org. • Strong SQL skills with experience building complex queries across large datasets; hands‐on experience with Snowflake. • Experience with HEX or a comparable collaborative notebook environment for analysis and stakeholder delivery. • Solid grounding in experiment design and statistical analysis — A/B testing, power analysis, significance testing, and awareness of common pitfalls like novelty effects and sample ratio mismatch. • Experience analyzing conversion funnels, user journeys, and event‐based behavioral data; comfortable thinking in cohorts, sessions, and sequences. • Strong communication skills with the ability to translate complex analytical findings into clear, actionable perspectives for PMs and product leadership. • Inquisitive mindset with a bias toward proactive investigation — you dig into the 'why' behind performance trends without being prompted. • Experience with a B2B API product, developer platform, marketplace, or technical product where the end user is a partner or business is a plus. • Familiarity with dbt or experience working closely with analytics engineering teams to build reusable data models is a plus. Why Join Us • Work on a genuinely complex data problem — booking events, pricing signals, API performance, and partner behavior at scale across 1M+ properties and 30M+ hotel nights processed. • Be embedded in a product team where your analysis directly shapes the roadmap — not just reports on it. • Join a data-driven culture that values curiosity, ownership, and continuous improvement, with real opportunities for growth and impact. Compensation Our compensation packages are based on several factors, including your experience, expertise, and location. In addition to a competitive base salary, all roles receive equity. Build readiness programs and learning paths that give CSMs working knowledge of identity security, including IAM, PAM, IGA, ITDR, and non-human and AI agent identities. Create clear, on-brand, visually engaging playbooks, presentations, and guides, and keep layout and branding consistent across formats. matches.d: About Engine Engine is the AI-native platform for intelligent travel. For a decade, Engine has built the proprietary technology and supply behind modern business travel, serving over 40,000 customers and nearly 2 million travelers, along with leading travel and AI companies that build on Engine 's infrastructure. One system powers business travel, group travel, human agents, and AI agents. That work has earned recognition as one of Fast Company's Best Workplaces for Innovators (2025), TravelTech's Reservation Platform of the Year (2026), and one of Built In's Best Places to Work (2020–2026). We're looking for bold, ambitious people to help redefine how businesses manage and experience travel. Working here, you can expect exponential growth, an ambitious pace, full ownership, and high-caliber colleagues who push you to do the best work of your career. Every hire raises the bar. Come outpace the ordinary and build the future of travel with us. Join Our Journey at Engine At Engine , we’re revolutionizing work travel. Our modern travel platform isn’t just about booking trips; it’s about transforming how businesses and their teams experience travel. From seamless booking with top airlines, hotels, and car rental providers to single-invoice billing and flexible trip modifications, we make travel easier to manage and better to experience. Engine is bringing its platform to the corporate-travel channel: travel management companies (TMCs) sign on, bring their corporate accounts, and book flights, hotels, and cars on Engine , direct bill, and Flex built in. Every TMC we sign, and every corporate account behind it, has to be configured, trained, and taken through its first booking before any of that value shows up. That work is this job. Your Mission: As Senior Lead OBT Implementation Manager, you'll own the path from signed agreement to live, booking TMC. You'll stand each agency up on Engine (GDS credentials, agency profile, queues, agent access), configure their corporate accounts (travelers, departments, travel policies, direct bill, Flex, custom fields, rewards), train their agents, and hold the timeline across several activations at once. You'll be our first dedicated implementer, which means you define how Engine implements TMCs: you build the playbook while you run it, set the standard for the implementers who follow you, and make sure the twentieth TMC goes live in a fraction of the time the second one did. What You’ll Do: Lead TMC implementations end to end: kickoff, discovery and scoping, project plan, risk log, go-live, and 30-day stabilization. Run several launches in parallel. Configure the platform for each TMC and its corporate clients: travel policy, approval flows, traveler profiles, display and content rules, Engine -only rates alongside TMC-negotiated rate programs, and chain rate-access approvals. Own GDS readiness across Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus: pseudo-city and agency setup, PNR structure, queue placement, profile sync, ticketing and mid-office handoff. Scope and deliver integrations: SSO, HRIS profile feeds, expense systems, duty of care, reporting and BI, commission tracking. Run UAT with TMC agents and corporate admins; triage defects with Product and Engine ering; make the go/no-go call. Build the implementation playbook: standard timelines, configuration templates, UAT scripts, and migration runbooks for corporates moving from legacy OBTs or from Engine .com self-serve onto Engine OBT+. Train agents, admins, and travel managers; produce written and video collateral they can reuse. Feed the roadmap: document TMC requirements and gaps, and carry the implementation lens into product reviews. Support Sales on pre-sale technical discovery, RFPs, and implementation scoping for enterprise TMCs. What You'll Bring to Engine : 7+ years in implementation, onboarding, or customer success, including time at a TMC or a travel technology company, and at least one role where you built the process rather than ran someone else's. Hands-on GDS experience in at least one of Sabre, Travelport, or Amadeus. Multi-GDS is a strong plus. Hands-on experience administering or supporting an online booking tool (Concur, Deem, Spotnana, or similar): profiles, policies, approvals, payment and billing setup. Strong written communication: you can turn a setup call into a reusable guide and a customer problem into a clear brief for Product. You've managed or mentored other implementers, or built an implementation function from the first hire. Comfort using AI tools to document, diagnose, and scale implementation content without sacrificing accuracy or depth. Bonus points You've worked inside a TMC and know the account-manager and agent workflows from the inside. Experience with direct bill, central billing, or corporate card setup in a travel program. Background in meetings and events or group travel. Applications for this role will be accepted through February 20 or until the role is filled. About The Role We are building AI into the way our go-to-market organization operates, sells, serves customers, and scales. This role exists to identify the highest-value opportunities for AI across the revenue engine, prove the business case with data, and build practical agents and workflows that improve productivity, decision quality, speed, and customer experience. This is a hands-on, business-facing builder role for someone who can operate across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and Revenue Operations. You will not simply receive a backlog. You will create one by finding friction, quantifying the opportunity, designing the solution, building and testing it, launching it with the field, and measuring whether it worked. The right person blends GTM judgment, AI fluency, data analysis, and enough technical depth to move from idea to production. This is not an advisory-only role and it is not a research role. It is for someone who can ship useful AI-enabled workflows that real teams adopt. Why This Role Matters Now AI is moving from experimentation to operating model. For GTM teams, that means the biggest advantage will not come from isolated tools or demos. It will come from thoughtful, governed workflows that help sellers prepare faster, managers coach with better insight, marketers target with more precision, and customer-facing teams act sooner on risk and opportunity. This role will help define how we responsibly apply AI across the revenue organization, improving scale without simply adding more manual effort or headcount. Example Use Cases Sales meeting prep agents that summarize account context, recent activity, open opportunities, risks, and recommended next actions. Account research workflows that combine internal data and approved external inputs to support prospecting and account planning. Renewal and churn risk agents that summarize signals, surface next-best actions, and support executive review processes. CRM hygiene and data quality automation, including enrichment, duplicate detection, field validation, and follow-up prompts. Post-call and post-meeting workflows that draft follow-ups, update CRM fields, identify action items, and flag coaching opportunities. Manager insight workflows that summarize pipeline movement, forecast changes, seller activity patterns, and execution risks. Marketing and sales alignment workflows that help connect campaign engagement to account prioritization and rep action. What You'll Do Find the opportunities Work across marketing, SDR/BDR, sales, customer success, and revenue operations to map how work actually gets done today: the manual steps, the handoffs, the queues, and the places where reps and managers lose time. Maintain a living, prioritized inventory of AI and automation opportunities across the GTM funnel, scored on impact, effort, risk, and data readiness. Pressure-test demand: separate problems that need AI from problems that need a process fix, a field on a record, or a better report. Bring recommendations forward with a clear thesis: what the problem costs today, what the intervention is, what it will cost, and what changes if we do it. Understand what drives the need Pull and analyze the data behind each opportunity: CRM, marketing automation, engagement and sequencing tools, support and CS platforms, product usage, and finance where relevant. Quantify the baseline before anything is built: volume, cycle time, conversion, cost per unit of work, error and rework rates. Define the success metric and the measurement method up front, and instrument the workflow so results are observable rather than anecdotal. Report on adoption and realized impact after launch, and be candid when something is not working. Build agents and workflows Design and build AI agents and automated workflows across multiple platforms: CRM-native automation, workflow and integration tools, agent-building platforms, and LLM APIs. Own the full build cycle: prototype, test against real data, pilot with a small user group, harden, launch, and iterate. Write and refine prompts, retrieval logic, tool definitions, and guardrails so agents behave reliably in production, not just in a demo. Handle the plumbing: data flows, integrations, field mapping, deduplication, error handling, and fallbacks to a human when an agent is out of its depth. Document what you build so it is supportable by someone other than you. Drive adoption Partner with GTM leaders and frontline teams so what you build gets used: training, enablement materials, office hours, and a feedback loop into the next iteration. Treat adoption as part of the deliverable. Workflows must be designed, launched, and measured in a way that makes them useful in the field, not just impressive in a demo. Keep it safe and governed Apply sensible guardrails around data handling, customer-facing output, and human review, particularly anything that touches prospects or customers directly. Work with IT, security, and legal on tool evaluation, data access, and vendor review. Track spend across AI tooling and model usage, and keep cost per outcome in view. What Success Looks Like First 90 days A documented map of GTM processes with the friction points and data gaps called out. A prioritized opportunity backlog with sizing and a recommended sequence. At least one automation or agent shipped to production and in daily use. First year A portfolio of agents and workflows live across more than one GTM function, with measured impact on cycle time, capacity, conversion, or cost. A repeatable intake-to-launch process others in the org can plug into. The team's default answer to 'could AI do this?' is grounded in evidence rather than opinion, because you supplied the evidence. Requirements 5+ years in revenue operations, sales operations, marketing operations, business systems, data analytics, automation, or applied AI, with strong exposure to GTM workflows. Demonstrated hands-on building: you have shipped AI-enabled workflows, automations, agents, or internal tools that real users adopted, and you can explain what you built, why it mattered, and how you measured impact. Strong data fluency, including SQL and advanced spreadsheet analysis, with the ability to size an opportunity, define baseline metrics, and build reporting that proves whether the work created value. Working knowledge of the GTM technology stack, including CRM platforms such as Salesforce or HubSpot, marketing automation, sales engagement, conversation intelligence, customer success, support, and reporting tools. Experience with LLM APIs, agent-building platforms, prompt design, structured outputs, retrieval or knowledge grounding, tool/function calling, and practical guardrails for production use. Experience with automation and integration tooling such as Zapier, Make, n8n, Workato, Tray.io, native CRM flows, webhooks, or API-based integrations. Comfort with light scripting or technical configuration, preferably Python or JavaScript, APIs, JSON, data transformation, and troubleshooting across systems. Practical understanding of evaluation, testing, monitoring, failure handling, privacy, security, and cost management for AI-enabled workflows. Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to ask good questions, translate between business needs and technical constraints, and challenge requests when the business case is weak. Self-directed and outcome-oriented. This role is defined by what you discover, build, launch, and improve, not only by what you are assigned. Nice to Have Experience in a B2B services, SaaS, MSP, technology, or complex sales environment. Familiarity with RAG, vector databases, embeddings, re-ranking, evaluation harnesses, or AI observability tools. Experience with data warehousing, reverse ETL, BI tooling, or analytics engineering. Experience supporting sales productivity, sales enablement, forecasting, renewal management, or customer lifecycle workflows. Prior exposure to AI SDR, conversation intelligence, forecasting, proposal generation, or account planning tools. This Role Is a Strong Fit If You like ambiguous, high-impact problems and can turn them into a practical sequence of work. You are comfortable challenging assumptions, but you do it constructively and with the goal of creating a better answer. You care about adoption as much as architecture. You can move between executive-level business context and detailed workflow design without losing the thread. You are energized by building the operating model for how AI becomes part of daily GTM execution. Originally posted on Himalayas

matches.d: About TJM Labs TJM Labs is building the digital workforce for pharmacy. Pharmacies are being asked to do more with fewer resources. Prescription volumes are growing, margins are tightening, and talented pharmacy teams spend too much of their day on repetitive operational work. We're changing that. TJM Labs builds AI-powered automation designed specifically for pharmacy. Our technology works within the systems pharmacies already use to automate repetitive workflows and create more capacity for pharmacists and pharmacy technicians to focus on the work that actually requires them. We're growing quickly, and successful implementation is one of the most important parts of delivering on that promise. That's where you come in. About the Role We're looking for an Implementation Lead to own the day-to-day execution of customer implementations from discovery through go-live and transition to ongoing support. This is a hands-on role at the intersection of pharmacy operations, project management, customer communication, and technology. You'll work in close partnership with a Customer Success Manager (CSM). The CSM owns the overall customer relationship, strategic alignment, and escalations. You own getting the implementation done. During implementation, you'll be the hub of the project. You'll coordinate customer and internal stakeholders, document how the pharmacy operates today, translate those workflows into clear requirements, maintain the implementation plan, manage communication and action items, own internal QA, and drive the project toward a successful go-live. You'll also own one of the most important safeguards in our implementation process: making sure what the pharmacy does, what we've documented, what we've asked our technical teams to build, and what we ultimately deliver all remain in sync. This isn't a role where you'll simply maintain a project plan and schedule meetings. You'll ask questions. You'll uncover exceptions. You'll document details. You'll chase down decisions. You'll test what we've built. You'll notice when something doesn't line up. You'll keep people accountable for commitments. And when a project starts drifting, you'll help get it back on course. You don't need to be an engineer or an AI expert. You do need to understand pharmacy operations and pharmacy management systems, be curious about technology, communicate exceptionally well, and be very good at turning complexity into clarity. What You'll Own 1. Day-to-Day Implementation Execution Once a customer enters implementation, you'll own the day-to-day work required to get them live. Establish and maintain the implementation plan, milestones, dependencies, and target go-live date. Lead implementation meetings, discovery sessions, and working sessions. Coordinate activities across the pharmacy, TJM technical teams, the CSM, and other internal stakeholders. Track decisions, action items, customer deliverables, risks, dependencies, and outstanding requirements. Follow up consistently to keep projects moving. Identify risks and blockers early and drive them toward resolution. Manage implementation changes and understand their impact on scope, requirements, and timelines. Keep projects on schedule and surface concerns before they become surprises. Coordinate go-live activities and the transition into ongoing support. At any point in the project, you should be able to answer: What needs to happen next to get this customer live? 2. Pharmacy Process Discovery & Documentation Before we can automate a pharmacy workflow, we need to understand exactly how that workflow operates today. You'll own creating and maintaining clear, accurate, and highly standardized documentation of each customer's current-state pharmacy processes before TJM automation is introduced. Lead structured workflow discovery with pharmacy stakeholders. Understand how work moves through the pharmacy today — including people, pharmacy management systems, other technology, handoffs, business rules, decision points, and dependencies. Document current-state processes using TJM's standard formats, terminology, and required level of detail. Capture exceptions and edge cases, not just the ideal or 'happy path.' Ask the follow-up questions needed to uncover assumptions, inconsistencies, and missing information. Validate documented workflows with the customer. Keep documentation current as new information is discovered or requirements change. Ensure important changes are reflected consistently across process documentation, requirements, implementation work, and testing. Help define how workflows should operate once TJM automation is introduced. Maintain a clear connection between how the pharmacy operates today, what the customer needs, and what TJM ultimately builds. Good documentation in this role isn't about writing more. It's about capturing the right information, in the right structure, so customers and TJM teams are operating from the same understanding. 3. Requirements & Technical Translation You'll help translate real-world pharmacy operations into clear requirements our technical teams can act on. You won't need to arrive as a technical business analyst, and you won't be expected to write code. We'll teach you TJM's technology, tools, and implementation methodology. Translate operational workflows into structured, actionable requirements. Identify relevant business rules, dependencies, expected outcomes, exceptions, and edge cases. Give technical teams the context they need to understand both what needs to happen and why. Answer questions and close gaps that arise as technical work progresses. Review proposed solutions against documented customer workflows and requirements. Identify when something being built doesn't appear to match what was documented or agreed upon. Keep requirements and documentation aligned as the implementation evolves. One of your most important responsibilities is preventing quiet drift between what the pharmacy needs, what we've documented, and what we're building. 4. Stakeholder Communication & Alignment You'll own communication across all stakeholders involved in the implementation. During implementation, you are the primary day-to-day implementation contact for the customer and the internal hub for project information. Establish and maintain a clear communication cadence. Lead customer implementation meetings and internal project discussions. Provide clear, concise updates on progress, timelines, decisions, risks, blockers, and next steps. Ensure decisions and changes are documented and communicated to everyone they affect. Make sure customer feedback and requirements reach the appropriate internal teams. Make sure internal decisions and updates make their way back to the appropriate customer stakeholders. Clearly communicate owners, commitments, and deadlines. Keep the CSM informed of project health, customer sentiment, risks, and important developments. Bring in the CSM when an issue requires strategic, relationship, commercial, or executive intervention. You own making sure the right people know the right things at the right time. 5. Internal QA & Customer Readiness You'll own the quality gate between work produced internally and what is presented to the customer. Customers should never be the first people to discover that something we built doesn't work as expected. Develop a clear understanding of what 'working correctly' means for each implementation. Validate completed work against documented customer requirements and workflows. Coordinate and execute internal testing before customer review. Test expected workflows as well as relevant exceptions and edge cases. Document defects, unexpected behavior, and gaps clearly enough for technical teams to act on them. Track identified issues through resolution. Retest fixes and confirm that previously identified issues have actually been resolved. Ensure the implementation reflects agreed-upon requirements and documented process changes. Determine when work is ready to move from internal QA to customer validation. Coordinate customer testing after internal QA is complete. Track customer feedback and issues through final resolution and go-live readiness. You don't need to be a software QA engineer. You do need to be methodical, curious, detail-oriented, and willing to test something until you're confident we're putting quality work in front of the customer. Your responsibility isn't simply to ask whether something was tested. It's to make sure we're confident in what we're asking the customer to test. 6. Continuous Improvement Implementation playbooks and processes. Pharmacy workflow documentation standards. Templates and project tools. Discovery practices. Requirements documentation. Internal QA and testing processes. Go-live readiness. Customer and internal communication. Handoffs between implementation and ongoing Customer Success. The goal isn't simply to complete implementations. It's to make our implementation process more consistent, predictable, efficient, and scalable every time we use it. You'll Probably Love This Role If... You get unusual satisfaction from turning chaos into a plan. You leave meetings knowing exactly who is doing what by when — and you've written it down. You notice the unanswered question everyone else skipped over. When someone says, 'and then we just process it normally,' your instinct is to ask, 'Okay, but what exactly does normally mean?' You understand that the way a workflow is supposed to happen and the way it actually happens at 4:45 on a Friday afternoon aren't always the same thing. You test things yourself instead of assuming that because someone said they're done, they're ready for the customer. You'd rather solve a problem than spend three days discussing who owns it. You like technology, but you're more interested in what it can do than technology for technology's sake. Why TJM Labs You'll join a fast-growing company working on a very real problem in healthcare.

matches.d: About Kaseya Kaseya is the leading provider of AI-powered IT management and cybersecurity software, serving Managed Service Providers (MSPs) and internal IT organizations worldwide. Our comprehensive platform helps organizations efficiently manage, secure, and automate their IT environments, driving operational efficiency and long-term business success. Backed by Insight Partners , a leading global software investor, Kaseya has experienced sustained double-digit growth and continues to expand its global footprint. Today, Kaseya supports customers in more than 20 countries and manages over 15 million endpoints worldwide. Founded in 2000, Kaseya was built by builders - and we're still building. We look for people who create rather than wait, who see a hard problem and lean in, and who treat challenges as raw material. At Kaseya, everyone plays a role in shaping the future of IT: whether you're in engineering, product, sales, marketing, customer support, or operations, your work helps protect, defend, and optimize IT environments across the globe. We're building teams that grow, perform, and make an impact. If you're driven by the itch to make things better - a product, a process, a career - you'll fit right in. At Kaseya, we don't just raise the bar. We build it. Position Summary The Business Process Lead, Digital & Service Experience owns the end-to-end design of our customer-facing digital and service experience — commerce, account self-service, our customer and partner portal, and the service function that supports customers across those channels. This position carries both live operational ownership of processes running in production today and the design and build of a genuine product-led digital commerce capability that does not yet exist. What exists today is an account and billing self-service surface; building an actual product-led commerce motion — trials, in-app purchase, and self-serve upgrade — is the central mandate of this role. Importantly, this role owns the business capabilities in this scope — their definition, design, decomposition, and governance — in close partnership with the business teams that operate the underlying functions day to day. It does not own those functions themselves; success depends on heavy partnership with business and technology leads rather than on direct authority. This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role: the person hired personally facilitates working sessions, maps processes, writes requirements, and stays engaged through delivery and adoption. It also sits within a newly created function whose standards are still being defined, and is a strong opportunity for someone who wants to build a practice rather than execute within an established one. Because this role spans live operational processes with service-level expectations attached and net-new capability design with no existing internal playbook, it requires someone comfortable holding both kinds of work simultaneously and deliberately protecting time for design work even when operational demands feel more urgent. Key Responsibilities Own and continuously maintain a detailed (L2/L3) decomposition of account self-service, portal, commerce, and service-experience capabilities, keeping documentation accurate as the operating model and systems landscape evolve, and using standards shared across the Business Process Lead team. Facilitate structured working sessions with the digital team and Customer Success leadership to document how processes work today and design how they should work going forward, producing process maps, documented decisions, and requirements a technical team can act on without extensive follow-up. Translate future-state process designs into system requirements, partner with Product Owners and Engineering Leads through design, build, and testing, and confirm that what gets delivered reflects the intended process design. Support two parallel delivery tracks — current, in-production systems and the next-generation platform build — correctly identifying which track an incoming request belongs to, and ensuring lessons learned in day-to-day operations are reflected back into documentation and forward-looking design work. Own change management, enablement, and adoption for process changes in this value stream — stakeholder impact assessment, readiness planning, training materials, and post-launch verification that new processes are being used as intended — and define and report the process performance metrics that show whether they are working. Hold and maintain documented agreements at shared boundaries with peer Business Process Leads, so handoffs between value streams are explicitly agreed rather than assumed. matches.t: Business Process Lead, Finance & Corporate Services
matches.why: Business process and operations role at an IT management company, though finance/back-office focus is less aligned with target interests.
matches.d: About Kaseya Kaseya is the leading provider of AI-powered IT management and cybersecurity software, serving Managed Service Providers (MSPs) and internal IT organizations worldwide. Our comprehensive platform helps organizations efficiently manage, secure, and automate their IT environments, driving operational efficiency and long-term business success. Backed by Insight Partners , a leading global software investor, Kaseya has experienced sustained double-digit growth and continues to expand its global footprint. Today, Kaseya supports customers in more than 20 countries and manages over 15 million endpoints worldwide. Founded in 2000, Kaseya was built by builders - and we're still building. We look for people who create rather than wait, who see a hard problem and lean in, and who treat challenges as raw material. At Kaseya, everyone plays a role in shaping the future of IT: whether you're in engineering, product, sales, marketing, customer support, or operations, your work helps protect, defend, and optimize IT environments across the globe. We're building teams that grow, perform, and make an impact. If you're driven by the itch to make things better - a product, a process, a career - you'll fit right in. At Kaseya, we don't just raise the bar. We build it. Position Summary The Business Process Lead, Finance & Corporate Services owns the end-to-end design of our financial and administrative back-office processes — financial close and reporting, procurement, tax, supply chain operations, hardware fulfillment, human resources operations, and sales compensation administration. This scope is intentionally broad rather than a single linear process flow, spanning several distinct domains that share a finance and administrative reporting line rather than a common process sequence. The role is the connective tissue between Finance, HR, and Supply Chain leadership and the technology teams that build supporting systems. Importantly, this role owns the business capabilities in this scope — their definition, design, decomposition, and governance — in close partnership with the business teams that operate the underlying functions day to day. It does not own those functions themselves; success depends on heavy partnership with business and technology leads rather than on direct authority. This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role: the person hired personally facilitates working sessions, maps processes, writes requirements, and stays engaged through delivery and adoption. It also sits within a newly created function whose standards and operating rhythm are still being defined. Deep specialist expertise in every domain within this scope is not expected; the ability to establish consistent standards, prioritize effectively, and drive improvement across genuinely different process areas is the core skill this role requires. Key Responsibilities Own and continuously maintain a detailed (L2/L3) decomposition of Record to Report, Direct Tax and Tax Compliance, Procure to Pay, Supply Chain Operations, hardware fulfillment, Hire to Retire, and Sales Compensation Management capabilities, keeping documentation accurate as the operating model and systems landscape evolve, and using standards shared across the Business Process Lead team. Facilitate structured working sessions with Finance, HR, Procurement, and Supply Chain stakeholders to document how processes work today and design how they should work going forward, producing process maps, documented decisions, and requirements a technical team can act on without extensive follow-up. Translate future-state process designs into system requirements, partner with Product Owners and Engineering Leads through design, build, and testing, and confirm that what gets delivered reflects the intended process design. Support two parallel delivery tracks — current, in-production systems and the next-generation platform build — correctly identifying which track an incoming request belongs to, and ensuring lessons learned in day-to-day operations are reflected back into documentation and forward-looking design work. Own change management, enablement, and adoption for process changes in this value stream — stakeholder impact assessment, readiness planning, training materials, and post-launch verification that new processes are being used as intended — and define and report the process performance metrics that show whether they are working. Hold and maintain documented agreements at shared boundaries with peer Business Process Leads, so handoffs between value streams are explicitly agreed rather than assumed. Own the capability design for sales compensation from an approved sales quota forward — plan administration, crediting rules, attainment calculation, dispute resolution, commission expense accrual, and the payout handoff to payroll — partnering with the Sales Compensation and Payroll teams who execute it. Own the capability design for hardware fulfillment — provisioning, warehouse and inventory management, returns, and warranty — and for Hire to Retire, including onboarding, self-service, HR helpdesk, absence, and performance management, partnering with the Supply Chain, Fulfillment Operations, HR, and People Operations teams who run them. Required Qualifications Hands-on experience designing or improving month-end close and record-to-report processes in a multi-entity ERP environment. 5+ years of experience in business process design, business analysis, business architecture, or operations in a relevant domain. Demonstrated experience decomposing business capabilities into detailed, multi-level structures. Strong facilitation skills with cross-functional business stakeholders, including experience working at a Controller or Finance director level. Experience translating business process requirements into system requirements for a technical delivery team, along with strong documentation habits. Preferred Qualifications Experience with physical fulfillment and supply chain process design — warehouse, inventory, returns processing, and warranty management. Sales compensation process design experience, including plan administration, crediting, attainment, dispute resolution, and commission accounting. Procure-to-pay process design experience, including intake, approval routing, supplier onboarding, and three-way match controls. Direct tax process and statutory reporting experience in a multi-jurisdiction environment. HR operations process design experience, including onboarding, self-service, helpdesk operations, and performance cycle management. Treasury and cash management process design experience. Experience with Oracle (accounting, inventory, and accounts payable modules), NetSuite, Oracle EPM, close management tooling such as FloQast, and incentive compensation platforms such as CaptivateIQ. Additional information Kaseya provides equal employment opportunity to all employees and applicants without regard to race, religion, age, ancestry, gender, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, veteran status, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.
